purpose: The footer under every marketing page: the link columns, then the social row beside the status indicator and the language select. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'site-footer', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `footer`, `brand`, `icon-button`, `status-indicator` and `select`. From `lg` the Azion mark leads the social row; below it the mark moves to the footer's signature band, so the icons get the row to themselves. The move is CSS only (`footer`'s `signature: 'compact'` hides the band from `lg`; the social-row mark shows from `lg`), so the page ends on the bottom bar from `lg` both in the server HTML and after hydration. The language select keeps its own value locally; its options are the labels the reader sees.
useWhen: As the last block of every marketing page.
avoidWhen: Inside the product console or the docs → compose `footer` directly.
For a closing ask above the footer → use `closing-call-to-action`.
related: footer` — the composition footer this section fills.
closing-call-to-action` — the band that sits right above it.
bestPractices: **Do** render it as the last child of the page shell, as is: it draws its own top rule, its frame and its closing bottom rule.
**Don't** wrap it in a bordered or padded `div` (`border-t`, `py-*`): the rules double and the frame drifts off the page column.
Use `kind: 'site'` under a framed marketing page, so the footer draws the page frame and closes on its bottom rule; the page above must not draw a bottom rule of its own.
Keep four link columns so the grid fills at `md`.

Set `external: true` on a link that leaves azion.com (Community, Status): it opens in a new tab, draws the external-link glyph after the label and tells assistive tech it opens a new tab. Never add the glyph or `target` yourself.
Give every social link a `label` that names the network, since the button shows only the glyph.
